title: Longest Balanced Stretch
statement:
`text` contains only `(` and `)`. A text is **balanced** if every `(` is closed by a later `)` and every `)` closes an earlier `(`, each used once, with the pairs properly nested (like in `(()())`).

Find the longest **contiguous stretch** of `text` that is balanced and return its length (`0` if there is none).

examples.explanation: The stretch `()` at the end is balanced; the first `(` has no partner.
The stretch `()()` in the middle is balanced; the first and last `)` have no partner.

hints.nudge: A balanced stretch cannot contain a closing bracket that has nothing to close. Where do such brackets split the text?
hints.pattern: A stack of positions: keep the position just BEFORE the current balanced stretch at the bottom, push the position of every `(`, and measure the length from the new top after each `)`.
hints.walkthrough: Checking every stretch for balance is O(n^3), or O(n^2) with a running counter. With a stack you can do it in one pass. Store positions, not brackets. At the bottom keep the position just before the current valid stretch (start with -1). Every `(` is pushed with its position. A `)` pops the top: if that was a `(`, they form a pair, and the balanced stretch ending here reaches back to the position that is NOW on top of the stack (everything between is balanced), so its length is i - top. If the pop removed the bottom marker, this `)` had no partner: it cannot be inside any balanced stretch, so push its position as the new bottom marker. The answer is the largest length seen. O(n) time and memory.
